International football competition

The **2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League** was the second season of the [UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "UEFA Europa Conference League"), Europe's tertiary club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA").

The [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_final "2023 UEFA Europa Conference League final") was played at [Fortuna Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Arena "Fortuna Arena") in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), Czech Republic.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-3) It was won by [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), who defeated [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") 2–1, and qualified for the [2023–24 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League") group stage as a result.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-4)

As the title holders, [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") qualified for the [2022–23 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League"). They were unable to defend their title after advancing to the [Europa League knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

## Association team allocation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Association team allocation")]

A total of 177 teams from 54 of the 55 [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") member associations (excluding Russia) participated in the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League. The association ranking based on the [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient") was used to determine the number of participating teams for each association:[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-regulations-5)

*   Associations 1–5 each had one team qualify.
*   Associations 6–17 (except [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union "Russian Football Union"))[[Note RUS]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_RUS) and 51–55 each had two teams qualify.
*   Associations 18–50 (except [Liechtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liechtenstein_Football_Association "Liechtenstein Football Association"))[[Note LIE]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_LIE) each had three teams qualify.
*   Liechtenstein had one team qualify as they organized only a domestic cup and no domestic league.[[Note LIE]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_LIE)
*   Moreover, 18 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Champions League and 25 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League were transferred to the Europa Conference League.

### Association ranking

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Association ranking")]

For the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League, the associations were allocated places according to their 2021 [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient"), which took into account their performance in European competitions from 2016–17 to 2020–21.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-country_coefficients-6)

Apart from the allocation based on the country coefficients, associations could have additional teams participating in the Europa Conference League, as noted below:

*   (UCL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Champions League
*   (UEL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Europa League

### Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Distribution")]

The following was the access list for this season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-7) In the default access list, the title holders of the Europa Conference League qualified for the Europa League group stage.

Due to the suspension of Russia for the 2022–23 European season, the following changes to the access list were made:

*   The cup winners of association 16 (Serbia) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 18 (Croatia) and 19 (Switzerland) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 30 to 39 (Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republic of Ireland, North Macedonia and Armenia) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Since several changes were made in the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") access list following the qualification of the [Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League") title holders to the Europa League group stage, the following changes to the access list were made:

*   The cup winners of association 17 (Czech Republic) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of association 20 (Greece) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 40 (Latvia) and 41 (Albania) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Moreover, in the default access list, originally 16 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path). However, since the Champions League title holders, [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), which were guaranteed a berth in the Champions League group stage, already qualified via their domestic league, only 15 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path) after the Champions League access list was rebalanced. As a result, only 16 teams entered the Champions Path second qualifying round (two of the losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were drawn to receive byes to the third qualifying round).

The labels in the parentheses show how each team qualified for the place of its starting round:

*   CW: Domestic cup winners

*   LC: League cup winners
*   RW: Regular season winners
*   PW: End-of-season Europa Conference League play-offs winners
*   UCL: Transferred from the Champions League 
    *   Q1: Losers from the first qualifying round
    *   PR: Losers from the preliminary round (F: final; SF: semi-finals)

*   UEL: Transferred from the Europa League 
    *   GS: Third-placed teams from the group stage
    *   PO: Losers from the play-off round
    *   CH/MP Q3: Losers from the third qualifying round (Champions/Main Path)

The second qualifying round, third qualifying round and play-off round were divided into Champions Path (**CH**) and Main Path (**MP**).

International football competition

The **2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League** was the second season of the [UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "UEFA Europa Conference League"), Europe's tertiary club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organised by [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA").

The [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_final "2023 UEFA Europa Conference League final") was played at [Fortuna Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Arena "Fortuna Arena") in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), Czech Republic.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-3) It was won by [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), who defeated [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") 2–1, and qualified for the [2023–24 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League") group stage as a result.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-4)

As the title holders, [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") qualified for the [2022–23 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League"). They were unable to defend their title after advancing to the [Europa League knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

## Association team allocation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Association team allocation")]

A total of 177 teams from 54 of the 55 [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") member associations (excluding Russia) participated in the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League. The association ranking based on the [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient") was used to determine the number of participating teams for each association:[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-regulations-5)

*   Associations 1–5 each had one team qualify.
*   Associations 6–17 (except [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union "Russian Football Union"))[[Note RUS]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_RUS) and 51–55 each had two teams qualify.
*   Associations 18–50 (except [Liechtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liechtenstein_Football_Association "Liechtenstein Football Association"))[[Note LIE]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_LIE) each had three teams qualify.
*   Liechtenstein had one team qualify as they organized only a domestic cup and no domestic league.[[Note LIE]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cnote_Note_LIE)
*   Moreover, 18 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Champions League and 25 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League were transferred to the Europa Conference League.

### Association ranking

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Association ranking")]

For the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League, the associations were allocated places according to their 2021 [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient"), which took into account their performance in European competitions from 2016–17 to 2020–21.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-country_coefficients-6)

Apart from the allocation based on the country coefficients, associations could have additional teams participating in the Europa Conference League, as noted below:

*   (UCL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Champions League
*   (UEL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Europa League

### Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Distribution")]

The following was the access list for this season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#cite_note-7) In the default access list, the title holders of the Europa Conference League qualified for the Europa League group stage.

Due to the suspension of Russia for the 2022–23 European season, the following changes to the access list were made:

*   The cup winners of association 16 (Serbia) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 18 (Croatia) and 19 (Switzerland) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 30 to 39 (Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republic of Ireland, North Macedonia and Armenia) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Since several changes were made in the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") access list following the qualification of the [Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League") title holders to the Europa League group stage, the following changes to the access list were made:

*   The cup winners of association 17 (Czech Republic) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of association 20 (Greece) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
*   The cup winners of associations 40 (Latvia) and 41 (Albania) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Moreover, in the default access list, originally 16 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path). However, since the Champions League title holders, [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), which were guaranteed a berth in the Champions League group stage, already qualified via their domestic league, only 15 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path) after the Champions League access list was rebalanced. As a result, only 16 teams entered the Champions Path second qualifying round (two of the losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were drawn to receive byes to the third qualifying round).

The **2022–23 season** was the [14th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_RB_Leipzig_seasons "List of RB Leipzig seasons") in the history of [RB Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Leipzig "RB Leipzig") and their seventh consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Bundesliga "2022–23 Bundesliga"), [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_DFB-Pokal "2022–23 DFB-Pokal"), [DFL-Supercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_DFL-Supercup "2022 DFL-Supercup") and [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League "2022–23 UEFA Champions League").

The **2022–23 season** was the [14th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_RB_Leipzig_seasons "List of RB Leipzig seasons") in the history of [RB Leipzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Leipzig "RB Leipzig") and their seventh consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Bundesliga "2022–23 Bundesliga"), [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_DFB-Pokal "2022–23 DFB-Pokal"), [DFL-Supercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_DFL-Supercup "2022 DFL-Supercup") and [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League "2022–23 UEFA Champions League").

The **2022–23 Eredivisie** was the 67th season of the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie"), the premier football competition in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 28 May 2023. As the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") started on 20 November, the last round before stoppage was held on 12–13 November. The league resumed games on 6 January.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-:0-1)

[Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") became the champions in round 32, beating [Go Ahead Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Ahead_Eagles "Go Ahead Eagles") 3–0 at [De Kuip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam") on 14 May 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-2)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

[Emmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Emmen "FC Emmen") (promoted after a one-year absence), [Volendam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volendam "FC Volendam") (promoted after a thirteen-year absence) and [Excelsior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Rotterdam "Excelsior Rotterdam") (promoted after a three-year absence) were promoted from the [2021–22 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Eerste_Divisie "2021–22 Eerste Divisie"). [Willem II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_II_(football_club) "Willem II (football club)") (relegated after eight years in the top flight), [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") (relegated after ten years in the top flight), and [Heracles Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heracles_Almelo "Heracles Almelo") (relegated after seventeen years in the top flight) were relegated to the [2022–23 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eerste_Divisie "2022–23 Eerste Divisie").

The **2022–23 Eredivisie** was the 67th season of the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie"), the premier football competition in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 28 May 2023. As the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") started on 20 November, the last round before stoppage was held on 12–13 November. The league resumed games on 6 January.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-:0-1)

[Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") became the champions in round 32, beating [Go Ahead Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Ahead_Eagles "Go Ahead Eagles") 3–0 at [De Kuip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam") on 14 May 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-2)

[Emmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Emmen "FC Emmen") (promoted after a one-year absence), [Volendam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volendam "FC Volendam") (promoted after a thirteen-year absence) and [Excelsior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Rotterdam "Excelsior Rotterdam") (promoted after a three-year absence) were promoted from the [2021–22 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Eerste_Divisie "2021–22 Eerste Divisie"). **Mees de Wit** (born 17 April 1998) is a Dutch professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-back "Left-back") for [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") club [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mees_de_Wit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

De Wit made his [Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eerste_Divisie "Eerste Divisie") debut for [Jong Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jong_Ajax "Jong Ajax") on 25 August 2017 in a game against [Fortuna Sittard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Sittard "Fortuna Sittard").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-1) He signed for Sporting's U-23 team for the 2018–19 season on 19 July 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-2) On 11 March 2019, Stefano van Delden, De Wit's agent in 2017 and 2018, made the news as he was suspected of threatening different members of the [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") board on several occasions during the period from 26 October 2017 to 25 September 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-3)

On 20 January 2020, de Wit moved to Spanish club [Orihuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orihuela_CF "Orihuela CF") on loan for the rest of the season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-4)

On 6 July 2021, he returned to the Netherlands and signed a contract with [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") for two years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-5)

De Wit performed exceptionally while playing for PEC Zwolle, leading to a five-year contract with [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") starting in July 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-6)

**Mees de Wit** (born 17 April 1998) is a Dutch professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-back "Left-back") for [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") club [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mees_de_Wit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

De Wit made his [Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eerste_Divisie "Eerste Divisie") debut for [Jong Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jong_Ajax "Jong Ajax") on 25 August 2017 in a game against [Fortuna Sittard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Sittard "Fortuna Sittard").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-1) He signed for Sporting's U-23 team for the 2018–19 season on 19 July 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-2) On 11 March 2019, Stefano van Delden, De Wit's agent in 2017 and 2018, made the news as he was suspected of threatening different members of the [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") board on several occasions during the period from 26 October 2017 to 25 September 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-3)

On 20 January 2020, de Wit moved to Spanish club [Orihuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orihuela_CF "Orihuela CF") on loan for the rest of the season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-4)

On 6 July 2021, he returned to the Netherlands and signed a contract with [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") for two years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-5)

De Wit performed exceptionally while playing for PEC Zwolle, leading to a five-year contract with [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") starting in July 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-6)
